title: Petting Your Dog May Protect You from Future Stress
paragraphs: Many dog owners say that spending time with their pets helps them relax. Now, a new study suggests that petting a dog may not help people calm down faster after a stressful experience, but it may help protect them from stress in the future.

The study was carried out by Vanessa Kaufmann, Annett Schirmer and Xiaoqin Cheng at the University of Innsbruck in Austria, and it was published in the journal Biological Psychology. It involved 64 dog owners and their dogs.

Each participant took part in two sessions. In each session, they first rested and then completed a stressful 10-minute test. They had to answer general knowledge questions quickly and count backward, while being told that they were being recorded and receiving only critical feedback from staff. After the test, they spent five minutes with their dog. In one session, the dog was free to move around, so the owners could touch it. In the other session, the dog was on a short leash, so the owners could talk to it and look at it, but could not touch it.
The researchers measured the participants' brain activity, heart rate and heart rate variability. The test clearly caused stress, raising participants' heart rates and changing their brain activity.

Contrary to what the researchers had expected, petting a dog did not help participants recover from stress any faster. However, there was a surprising result. The participants who had touched their dogs showed a weaker stress response when they took the second test. Their heart rates were slower, and they reported a greater sense of control. Participants who could not touch their dogs did not show this change.

The researchers noted some limitations. This result came from an additional analysis, so it needs to be confirmed by further studies. Most of the participants were women, and all were tested with their own dogs.
The researchers also stressed that the dog's comfort matters, saying that physical contact should always be wanted and positive for both sides.
